title: Could a four-day working week work
titleChinese: 每周四天工作日，可行吗？
paragraphs: People in the UK work longer hours than anyone else in the European Union but are far from the most productive. According to the Trades Union Congress, a UK body that brings together 49 member unions to improve their working conditions, employees in Denmark are 24% more productive per hour but work four hours fewer per week. 'Britain's long-hours culture… is robbing workers of a decent home life and time with their loved ones. Overwork, stress and exhaustion have become the new normal,' says TUC General Secretary Frances O'Grady. They want businesses to cut the standard working week from five days to four. But would a four-day week work?

It does for Rich Leigh, founder of a Gloucester-based PR business. Staff there work Monday to Thursday, 9am – 5:30pm, but still get paid the same as before. In an interview with the BBC, Leigh claims it makes the staff happier, which leads to better, more productive work. After a year, earnings and profits are up and sick days have halved.

The 4 Day Week Campaign also believes a shorter week would benefit everyone. They claim that it would, among other things, more evenly distribute work between the overworked and the underemployed. They estimate that around 30 UK businesses operate a 'four day, same pay' system.

However, not everyone is convinced. One of the UK's leading charities, the Wellcome Trust, conducted an organisation-wide consultation into whether a four-day week would fit. They decided against it. 'Many employees worried about their five-day workloads being compressed into just four days and some raised concerns that the time and energy used to implement a four-day week would distract the charity from its core work,' says Ed Whiting, director of policy at the Trust.

So does a four-day working week work or not? Clearly it suits some… but not everyone. "We've got a lot to do before it can work for different sectors," says Emelia Quist from the Federation of Small Businesses in a BBC interview. 'Social care needs people present 24/7. How can we ensure those industries can work a four-day week?' she adds. Until we can answer questions like these, there's clearly more work to be done.

vocabulary.entry: productive /prəˈdʌktɪv/ adj. 高效的；多产的
vocabulary.example: She is one of the most productive members of the team.
vocabulary.translation: 她是团队中工作效率最高的成员之一。

vocabulary.entry: Trades Union Congress /ˌtreɪdz ˈjuːniən ˈkɒŋɡres/ 英国工会大会（TUC）
vocabulary.example: The Trades Union Congress has called for better working rights for part-time workers.
vocabulary.translation: 英国工会大会呼吁保障兼职人员的劳动权益。

vocabulary.entry: long-hours culture /ˌlɒŋ ˈaʊəz ˈkʌltʃə/ 超长工作时长文化
vocabulary.example: The long-hours culture in this industry often leads to employees' burnout.
vocabulary.translation: 该行业的超长工作时长文化常常导致员工过劳。

vocabulary.entry: rob sb of sth /rɒb sb ɒv sth/ 剥夺某人某物
vocabulary.example: The accident robbed him of his ability to walk.
vocabulary.translation: 那场事故剥夺了他行走的能力。

vocabulary.entry: decent /ˈdiːsnt/ adj. 体面的；像样的
vocabulary.example: He earns a decent salary to support his family.
vocabulary.translation: 他的薪水不错，足以养家糊口。

vocabulary.entry: exhaustion /ɪɡˈzɔːstʃən/ n. 疲惫；精疲力竭
vocabulary.example: She collapsed from exhaustion after working for 12 hours straight.
vocabulary.translation: 连续工作12小时后，她因精疲力竭而倒下。

vocabulary.entry: standard working week /ˈstændəd ˈwɜːkɪŋ wiːk/ 标准工作周
vocabulary.example: The standard working week in this country is 40 hours.
vocabulary.translation: 该国的标准工作周为40小时。

vocabulary.entry: PR business /ˌpiː ˈɑː ˈbɪznəs/ 公关公司
vocabulary.example: He runs a successful PR business in the city center.
vocabulary.translation: 他在市中心经营着一家生意红火的公关公司。

vocabulary.entry: profit /ˈprɒfɪt/ n. 利润；收益
vocabulary.example: The company made a huge profit last year.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司去年获得了巨额利润。

vocabulary.entry: halve /hɑːv/ v. 减半；把……分成两半
vocabulary.example: The government plans to halve the unemployment rate in five years.
vocabulary.translation: 政府计划在五年内将失业率降低一半。

vocabulary.entry: distribute /dɪˈstrɪbjuːt/ v. 分配；分发
vocabulary.example: The teacher distributed the textbooks to the students at the beginning of the term.
vocabulary.translation: 学期开始时，老师把课本分发给了学生。

vocabulary.entry: overworked /ˌəʊvəˈwɜːkt/ adj. 工作过度的；超负荷工作的
vocabulary.example: Overworked doctors often don't have enough time to rest.
vocabulary.translation: 超负荷工作的医生往往没有足够的时间休息。

vocabulary.entry: underemployed /ˌʌndərɪmˈplɔɪd/ adj. 未充分就业的
vocabulary.example: Many underemployed graduates are looking for better job opportunities.
vocabulary.translation: 许多未充分就业的毕业生正在寻找更好的工作机会。

vocabulary.entry: consultation /ˌkɒnslˈteɪʃn/ n. 咨询；调研
vocabulary.example: The company will hold a staff consultation about the new policy.
vocabulary.translation: 公司将就新政策开展员工调研。

vocabulary.entry: compress /kəmˈpres/ v. 压缩；精简
vocabulary.example: We need to compress the report into three pages.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要把这份报告压缩到三页以内。

vocabulary.entry: implement /ˈɪmplɪment/ v. 实施；执行
vocabulary.example: The government will implement new regulations to protect the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 政府将实施新的法规来保护环境。

vocabulary.entry: distract sb from sth /dɪˈstrækt sb frəm sth/ 使某人分心；使某人偏离某事
vocabulary.example: Don't distract me from my work.
vocabulary.translation: 别让我在工作时分心。

vocabulary.entry: core work /kɔː wɜːk/ 核心工作

vocabulary.translation: 该部门的核心工作是研发新产品。

vocabulary.entry: sector /ˈsektə/ n. 行业；部门

vocabulary.translation: 教育行业今年获得了更多资金投入。

vocabulary.entry: social care /ˈsəʊʃl keə/ 社会关怀行业
vocabulary.example: Social care plays an important role in helping the elderly and disabled.
vocabulary.translation: 社会关怀行业在帮扶老人和残疾人方面发挥着重要作用。

vocabulary.entry: 24/7 /ˌtwenti ˈfɔː ˈsevən/ 全天候；日夜不停（twenty-four seven）
vocabulary.example: The emergency hotline operates 24/7.
vocabulary.translation: 这条紧急热线全天候开通。

vocabulary.translation: 这种新方法并非适用于所有类型的项目。
